title: The shell mints 16-hex capture ids the contract refuses, so no card shows its screenshot
body:
## Summary
The desktop shell mints capture ids as `cap_` plus 16 hex digits, while `contracts/ids.py` accepts a capture id only with exactly 12, so the daemon reads every real capture the desktop sends as no capture and every card is filed without its screenshot.

## Description
`Store::put_capture` files a capture through `Store::set`, whose `KeyMode::Minted("cap")` key calls `mint_id`, which formats `{prefix}_{:016x}` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/store.rs:211, :390, :801-819). `takeCapture` hands that id to the turn request as `capture_id` (apps/desktop/src/lib/hands.ts:124-128, apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1247, apps/desktop/src/stores/voice.ts:495). The daemon reads it with `capture_id_from`, which keeps it only when `ids.is_id("capture", ...)` (src/athena/daemon/routes.py:627-636), and `is_id` demands exactly `ID_SUFFIX_HEX["capture"]` = 12 hex digits (src/athena/contracts/ids.py:42, :78). A 16-digit id is "a malformed field" and is dropped silently, so the card carries `capture_id: null` and the desktop renders it with no shot (apps/desktop/src/companion/model.ts:778). README 3.5 ("the user sees the page the proposal is about and not a description of it") never happens in the real window. `approvals.create` would also refuse the shell's shape outright (src/athena/core/approvals.py:380). The store.rs comment claims ids crossing the seam are minted by `ids.ts`, which does not exist (fixed in ids.py's docstring this round, 6f43cf0). Registry ipc-contract, type drift and "the generated declaration must describe what the transport delivers". Fixed looks like: one width for a capture id on both sides - the shell mints 12 hex as the table says (the contract is the authority, AGENTS.md "ids in one place per language") - and a test in tests/contracts that reads store.rs's mint format and the Minted prefix and holds them to ID_PREFIXES/ID_SUFFIX_HEX.

## Flow
- Desktop: a gated request on the focused tab -> `takeCapture` -> `hands_call page_screenshot` -> store mints `cap_<16 hex>`
- -> `POST /run {capture_id: "cap_0123456789abcdef"}` -> `capture_id_from` -> `is_id("capture")` False -> None
- -> the gate files the card with capture_id None -> the card shows no screenshot
- Build order: the parity test (red on today's tree), then the Rust mint width (or, the other way, the Python width plus the 12-hex fixtures in tests/harness/test_capture_on_card.py, tests/daemon/test_gated_origins.py, tests/channels/test_voice_gateway.py)

## Expected impact
Everyone approving a gated page action in the desktop: the card gains the screenshot it was designed to carry; measured as the share of shell-minted capture ids the daemon keeps (0 of 1 today). Could break: captures already in a user's store keep 16-digit ids; they are swept by size and no card ever referenced one, so nothing reads them.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a card carries the screenshot the shell took for it
Before: probe, this round: `capture_id_from({"capture_id": "cap_0123456789abcdef"})` -> None; `is_id("capture", ...)` False; `kind_of(...)` None; a Python-minted `cap_<12 hex>` is kept
After: predicted - the shell-shaped id is kept and reaches the card; the parity test green
Method: probe for Before; the fix lives in apps/desktop/src-tauri (store.rs) or in four test files of three other contexts, none in this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
probe (2026-10-16): shell-minted cap_0123456789abcdef -> None False None; python-minted -> cap_527db8c73610
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/store.rs:211 key_mode: KeyMode::Minted("cap")
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/store.rs:819 format!("{prefix}_{:016x}", hasher.finish())
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/store.rs:801-803 "Every id that crosses the Python/TypeScript seam is minted by `ids.ts` instead" (no ids.ts exists)
src/athena/contracts/ids.py:42 ID_SUFFIX_HEX = dict.fromkeys(ID_PREFIXES, 12) | {"episode": 8}
src/athena/daemon/routes.py:634 if isinstance(raw, str) and ids.is_id("capture", raw.strip()):
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1247 ...(taken.id ? { capture_id: taken.id } : {})
tests using a 12-hex capture fixture: tests/harness/test_capture_on_card.py:14, tests/daemon/test_gated_origins.py:118, tests/channels/test_voice_gateway.py:698, tests/contracts/test_channel.py:74
instrument: tests/contracts/test_ids.py: read apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/store.rs (comments stripped), take the KeyMode::Minted prefix for captures and the hex width in mint_id's format, and assert prefix + '_' == ID_PREFIXES['capture'] and width == ID_SUFFIX_HEX['capture'] (red today: 16 vs 12); plus a daemon route test posting a store-shaped capture id and asserting the filed card carries it.

title: A page_origin of http://localhost.evil.example passes the https-or-localhost rule
body:
## Summary
`HostManifest.validate` accepts any `page_origin` that starts with `http://localhost`, so a plain-http remote origin such as `http://localhost.evil.example` passes the rule meant to admit only TLS origins and the local machine; the desktop's `registrable` copies the same prefix test.

## Description
src/athena/contracts/manifest.py:212-219 checks `page_origin.startswith("https://") or page_origin.startswith("http://localhost")`. A prefix match on the scheme-and-host string admits any host that begins with `localhost` - `http://localhost.evil.example`, `http://localhostile.net` - over plain http, which is exactly the class the rule exists to refuse (a page whose tools a network attacker can rewrite in transit). It also admits `https://` with no host. apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.ts:130-132 `registrable` is a hand copy of the same test ("The daemon refuses any other page_origin, so none is offered"), so tightening one side alone makes the desktop offer a manifest the daemon refuses. Registry ipc-contract (one rule, two copies). Fixed looks like: parse the origin; https with a non-empty host, or http whose host is exactly `localhost` (optionally `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`, decided once); the same rule in manifest.ts, with a parity case list both sides test.

## Flow
- A user browses to http://localhost.evil.example (any plain-http site whose name starts with "localhost")
- -> inject.js lists the page's tools -> manifestOf -> registrable(origin) true -> POST /manifest
- -> HostManifest.validate: no problem -> the page's tools are merged and the session pinned to it
- Build order: a shared case table (accept/refuse) in tests/contracts/test_manifest.py and apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.test.ts, then both predicates

## Expected impact
Defence in depth for the one person who opens such a page; measured as remote plain-http origins admitted (2 of 2 probes today). Could break: a developer serving examples on a hostname like `localhost.test` would need it named; examples use http://localhost:300x, which stays admitted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - only TLS origins and the local machine can register tools
Before: probe, this round: `HostManifest(app_id="x", page_origin="http://localhost.evil.example").validate()` -> []; `page_origin="https://"` -> []
After: predicted - both refused with the page_origin problem; http://localhost:3001 and https://ledger.test still accepted
Method: probe for Before; not built because the desktop mirror must follow and apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.ts is outside this round's paths (the brief's rule for a mirrored contract)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
probe (2026-10-16): HostManifest(app_id='x', page_origin='http://localhost.evil.example').validate() -> []
probe: HostManifest(app_id='x', page_origin='https://').validate() -> []
src/athena/contracts/manifest.py:213-214 self.page_origin.startswith("https://") or self.page_origin.startswith("http://localhost")
apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.ts:131 return origin.startsWith("https://") || origin.startsWith("http://localhost");
instrument: One accept/refuse table (http://localhost:3001, https://ledger.test accept; http://localhost.evil.example, http://localhostile.net, https://, http://example.com refuse) asserted against HostManifest.validate in tests/contracts/test_manifest.py and against registrable in apps/desktop/src/lib/manifest.test.ts; before: 2 refuse cases admitted on both sides.

title: ToolEntry admits a connector entry with no executor, which the gate then treats as a host tool
body:
## Summary
`ToolEntry.__post_init__` requires an executor for a core tool and forbids one for a host tool, but says nothing about a connector tool, so a `connector:<id>` entry with no executor is constructible and the gate hands its call to the surface as if a page would run it.

## Description
src/athena/contracts/registry.py:10-13 states the rule: a connector tool "does have an executor, and it runs in the daemon's process behind the vault". `__post_init__` enforces the core and host halves only (src/athena/contracts/registry.py:306-309). `PolicyHook._execute` reads "no executor" as "a host tool; the page runs it" (src/athena/harness/hooks.py:321-324), so an executor-less connector entry would be emitted as a `tool.call` instruction to a surface that has no page for `connector:<id>` and its answer would never come. Production builds connector entries only through `Catalog.merge_connector`, which always binds `_connector_executor` (src/athena/core/catalog.py:312), and the daemon's POST /manifest refuses `origin_kind: connector` (src/athena/daemon/routes.py:504) - but `Catalog.merge_manifest` itself accepts a connector-kind manifest with `executor_for=lambda tool: None` (src/athena/core/catalog.py:296), so the contract is the only structural guard, and it is missing. Fixed looks like: `if parsed.kind == "connector" and self.executor is None: raise ValueError(...)`, which `_merge` already turns into a refused manifest.

## Flow
- `Catalog.merge_manifest(HostManifest(app_id="gmail", origin_kind="connector", tools=[...]))` from any in-process caller
- -> `_merge` -> `ToolEntry(origin="connector:gmail", executor=None)` accepted
- -> a turn calls `connector.gmail.send` -> `_execute` returns None -> the lane waits for a page that does not exist
- Build order: the contract test (red), the guard, the one test fixture that builds such an entry

## Expected impact
Nobody today (no production path builds one); it closes the contract hole that the daemon route alone covers. Measured as executor-less connector entries the contract admits (1 of 1 today). Could break: tests/harness/test_cross_tab.py:127 builds `make_entry("connector.gmail.send", origin="connector:gmail")` with no executor and would need one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the registry row refuses the state its own docstring says cannot exist
Before: by reading the code, `ToolEntry(name="connector.g.x", origin="connector:g", cls=ToolClass.GATED)` constructs; `merge_manifest` of a connector-kind manifest merges executor-less entries
After: predicted - both refused (ValueError / CatalogError); every merge_connector entry unchanged
Method: simulation - not built because the coupled fixture is tests/harness/test_cross_tab.py, another context's file, and the rule this round runs under keeps a fix inside its write set
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/contracts/registry.py:12 a connector tool ... does have an executor
src/athena/contracts/registry.py:306-309 only core (needs one) and host (must have none) are checked
src/athena/harness/hooks.py:321-324 if entry.executor is None: # A host tool ... return None
src/athena/core/catalog.py:296 merge_manifest -> self._merge(manifest, executor_for=lambda tool: None)
tests/harness/test_cross_tab.py:127 make_entry("connector.gmail.send", ToolClass.AUTO, origin="connector:gmail")  (no executor)
instrument: tests/contracts/test_registry.py: ToolEntry(name='connector.g.x', origin='connector:g', cls=GATED) must raise ValueError naming the executor, and tests/core: Catalog.merge_manifest of an origin_kind='connector' manifest must raise CatalogError; red on today's tree; give tests/harness/test_cross_tab.py:127 an executor.

title: adopt.ts names a contract file that does not exist and types LaneEvent.lane non-null
body:
## Summary
The desktop's adopt wire module says it mirrors `src/athena/adopt/contract.py`, which does not exist (the contract is `src/athena/contracts/adopt.py`), and it types `adopt.lane`'s `lane` as always present where the contract allows `None`.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt.ts:2 "mirrors src/athena/adopt/contract.py (ADR 0097)" - `git ls-files src/athena/adopt` has no contract.py; the authority is src/athena/contracts/adopt.py, which tests/contracts/test_adopt_parity.py now holds the module to field for field (112b358). The same parity pass found one nullability difference it does not pin: `LaneEvent.lane: Lane | None = None` (src/athena/contracts/adopt.py:154) against `{ kind: "adopt.lane"; seq: number; lane: Lane }` (apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt.ts:95). Every producer sets it (src/athena/adopt/lanes.py:149, :160, :189), so nothing breaks today; a producer that emitted the default would hand the desktop a null its type says cannot come. Registry ipc-contract: "generated type promises values the wire cannot carry", in reverse. Fixed looks like: the header names the real path, and either the desktop types `lane: Lane | null` and handles it, or the contract makes `lane` required (a kw_only field) - then a nullability case joins test_adopt_parity.

## Flow
- A reader opens adopt.ts to find the authority -> follows src/athena/adopt/contract.py -> no such file
- A future producer emits LaneEvent() -> {"lane": null} on the wire -> the desktop's typed reader dereferences it

## Expected impact
Desktop maintainers reading the seam; measured as stale path claims (1) and unpinned nullability differences (1). Could break: nothing for the comment; a required field changes the dataclass's construction order.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mirror names its authority and agrees with it on what can be null
Before: 1 nonexistent path named; 1 nullability difference (git ls-files; read of both declarations)
After: 0 and 0, with a nullability case in the parity test
Method: probe for Before (the grep and the two declarations); the edit is in apps/desktop, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt.ts:2 mirrors src/athena/adopt/contract.py (ADR 0097)
git ls-files src/athena/adopt | grep contract -> nothing
src/athena/contracts/adopt.py:154 lane: Lane | None = None
apps/desktop/src/lib/adopt.ts:95 | { kind: "adopt.lane"; seq: number; lane: Lane }
src/athena/adopt/lanes.py:149,160,189 LaneEvent(lane=...) always set
instrument: Extend tests/contracts/test_adopt_parity.py with the nullability rule events.test.ts uses for channel.py (a field Python types X | None is the one the mirror lets be null, and no other); red today on adopt.lane; plus git grep 'adopt/contract.py' -- apps = 0.
